newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says new team will target younger market.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says new team will target younger market.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday it will set up a project team on August 1 to develop vehicles targeting a younger market, as it seeks to shore up its domestic market share.
The new team, whose 40 members will include 10 from outside the company, will focus on targeting people under the age of 30, Toyota said in a statement.
Toyota decided to form the team as the company felt it was gaining a reputation for being quite conservative, a Toyota spokeswoman said.
Toyota, Japan's top car maker, lags behind rival Honda Motor Co in the under-30 market, industry sources said.

Toyota has just under a 40 percent share of Japan's overall domestic car market, but that falls below 30 percent in the younger market because Toyota is less competitive in recreational vehicles, the sources said.
Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda told a news conference in the central Japanese city of Nagoya on Friday that his company was aiming to boost domestic sales back over the 40 percent mark.
Its domestic market share fell to 39.7 percent in 1996 from 40 percent the year before. It was the first time the top car maker's share fell short of 40 percent in 14 years.
